vin.title: This car, verified
vin.teaser: We ran this car's VIN through the same decode logic behind our Cutover tool, then cross-checked it against NHTSA's own public database. Both agree on every field that overlaps: Fremont-built, model year 2024, Dual Motor AWD. Here's the breakdown, position by position.

specs.title: The full spec sheet
specs.teaser: 4.8 seconds to 60, 310 miles EPA range, a 250 kW peak charge rate, and the color story you probably don't know: your black paint wasn't the free color in 2024. Stealth Grey was.

lineup.title: Where Long Range AWD sits in the lineup
lineup.teaser: Tesla's trim ladder is mostly a range-and-performance ladder, not a features ladder: the touchscreen, heated seats, and glass roof on your car are the same ones on every other 2024 Model Y.

history.title: Production history & the "best-selling car" claim
history.teaser: Model Y really was the best-selling vehicle on Earth in 2023: the first EV ever to hold that title. 2024 is genuinely a coin flip depending on whose numbers you trust. We checked both.

juniper.title: Pre-Juniper vs. Juniper: what this car has and doesn't
juniper.teaser: Tesla redesigned Model Y in 2025. This car predates it: here's exactly what changed, so a buyer knows what they're not getting (and what they are).

costs.title: What this car costs to run
costs.teaser: Home charging is a clear, durable win over gas. Supercharging's advantage is a lot thinner than the internet tells you. At today's prices, it can vanish entirely. Here's the real math for this car's 24,000–28,000 mi/year plan.

fleet.title: What it actually replaced
fleet.teaser: The RAV4-class comparison above is a hypothetical car. These three are the ones really in the driveway between September 2025 and August 2026: a 13 mpg work van, a 15 mpg V8 SUV, and a 20 mpg minivan. Measured against the fleet this car genuinely displaced, the math stops being close.

resale.title: Resale value & warranty: the honest version
resale.teaser: Model Y depreciation genuinely runs worse than the segment average, mostly because of Tesla's own price cuts. The warranty, on the other hand, is good news: it transferred to you automatically.

software.title: FSD, Autopilot, software & connectivity: what's running
software.teaser: This car is running FSD (Supervised) v14.3.6, and it's confirmed active on the current owner's account: they added the $99/month subscription themselves, so there's no guessing here like there is on a lot of used-Tesla purchases. The car is also on Premium Connectivity, with the owner's phone set up as a key.

usecases.title: Real-world use cases
usecases.teaser: Specs and a VIN decode only go so far. This is what owning this specific car actually looks like against real routines and real trips, with real numbers attached: the daily commute, a weekend road trip, winter range, insurance, and a real three-jobs-one-car schedule. Built to hold more over time.

fun.title: The fun stuff: Toybox, Easter eggs & only-Tesla tricks
fun.teaser: Emissions Testing Mode is still there. So is Caraoke, Mars Mode, and a genuine SpaceX docking simulator. The Atari games, though, are gone from your car specifically. Here's the current, verified list.

accessories.title: Accessories that earn their keep
accessories.teaser: Tesla ships this car with almost no cargo organization and no floor protection. Here's what owners buy first, and a few places to compare before you do.

appliance.title: Living with a transportation appliance
appliance.teaser: This car's owner coined that phrase because it fits: mainly a commuter, built to run every day without asking for much back.

community.title: Community & resources
community.teaser: Forums, third-party apps that go further than the Tesla app, what it actually takes to self-host TeslaMate, and the handful of YouTube channels the community trusts for straight information over hype.
